tictactoe.intro: Take turns placing your mark on the 3×3 board.

sections.title: How to win
items: Get three of your marks in a row — across, down or diagonally.
If the board fills up with no line, it's a draw.

avalon.intro: The agents try to complete three operations. Moles hide among them and try to make three operations fail.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: A team game of hidden identities. Agents try to complete operations; moles hide among them and sabotage.
items: Each player is secretly an Agent or a Mole. Moles know each other; most agents know nobody.
The game lasts up to five operations. Agents need three to succeed; moles need three to fail.
Agents who reach three successes still have to survive the Hitman's guess at the Handler.
Moles also win if five proposed teams in a row are rejected.
Roles are dealt at random and depend on the number of players (see Setup).

round.title: Each round
items: Leader: the player with the crown proposes a team of the size shown on the track.
Vote: everyone approves or rejects. Votes are revealed together once all are in.
A strict majority approves the team. A tie is a rejection.
Rejected: the crown passes to the next player, who proposes a new team. Five rejections in a row and the moles win.
Approved: each team member secretly plays Success or Fail — hold the card for 2 seconds. Agents can only play Success; moles may play either.
The cards are revealed without names. One Fail fails the operation (Operation 4 needs two with 7 or more players).
The crown moves on and the next operation begins.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Eight roles in total. Which ones are in a game depends on the player count — see Setup.

setup.title: Setup
setup.intro: Roles in play and team size for each of the five operations, by number of players.

ending.title: The ending
items: Three failed operations: the moles win at once.
Three successful operations: the moles are revealed and may talk it over. The Hitman then names one agent as the Handler.
If the Hitman is right, the moles steal the win. If wrong, the agents win.
When the game ends, everyone's role is shown.

more.title: More rules
items: Discussion happens out loud. Anyone may lie about anything — but never show your screen.
Your role card is face down until you tap it. Tap again to hide it.
Team votes are public once revealed and stay in History. Operation cards are never linked to a player — only the number of Fails is shown.
Handler: hint, don't announce. The more obvious you are, the easier the Hitman's job.
A mole on a team doesn't have to play Fail. Playing Success can build trust.
If a player leaves mid-game, the game ends for everyone and all roles are revealed.

merlin.note: Stay hidden. If the agents win three operations, the Hitman wins the game by naming you.

coup.intro: Everyone runs two stalls — two hidden cards. Bluff, challenge and block until you are the last player with a card left. The deck has 15 cards: 3 each of Boss, Enforcer, Pickpocket, Fixer and Auntie.

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: Everyone runs a crew of two hidden cards. Bluff, challenge and block until you're the last player with a card left.
items: Setup: each player gets 2 face-down cards and $2. The deck has 15 cards — 3 each of Boss, Enforcer, Pickpocket, Fixer and Auntie.
On your turn you take exactly one action. Some actions need a role — but you may claim a role you don't have.
After you announce an action, the other players may challenge your claim or block the action.
A card you lose is turned face up. Lose both and you're out.
The last player with a card wins.
Everyone's cash and lost cards are public. Face-down cards and the deck are secret.

roles.title: Roles
roles.intro: Five roles, three copies of each. A role gives you a special action, lets you block something, or both.

actions.title: Actions
actions.intro: Take one per turn. "Needs" is the role you must claim — truthfully or not.

challenges.title: Challenges
items: Whenever a player claims a role — to take an action or to block one — any other player may challenge.
Everyone else chooses Challenge or Allow. The first challenge settles it.
If it was a bluff: the bluffer loses a card. A bluffed action doesn't happen; a bluffed block fails and the action goes through.
If it was true: the challenger loses a card. The proven card is shuffled back into the deck and replaced with a new one, so the hand stays secret.
Day Job, Borrow and Shut Down claim no role, so they can't be challenged.
Once you tap Allow, you can't challenge that claim any more.

blocks.title: Blocks
items: Borrow can be blocked by any player claiming Boss.
Pickpocket can be blocked only by its target, claiming Pickpocket or Fixer.
Rough Up can be blocked only by its target, claiming Auntie.
A block is a claim, so anyone may challenge it. If the block was a bluff, the blocker loses a card and the action still happens.
A successful block cancels the action. Money already paid is not returned.
Day Job, Collect Rent, Swap and Shut Down can't be blocked.

more.title: More rules
items: With $10 or more at the start of your turn, you must Shut Down someone.
Rough Up costs $3 up front. You get it back only if you're caught bluffing the Enforcer — not if the action is blocked.
Double loss: bluff Auntie against a Rough Up and get challenged, and you lose one card for the bluff and one for the Rough Up.
With two cards, you choose which one to lose. With one card left there's no choice.
When you're out, your cash is gone and you only watch.
Two players: whoever goes first starts with $1 instead of $2.
If a player leaves mid-game, the game ends for everyone with no winner.
Tap your cards to flip them face down when someone might peek.

effects.steal: Take $2 from another player (or whatever they have, if less).
effects.exchange: Draw 2 cards from the deck, then return any 2. Changes your roles in secret.
effects.assassinate: Choose a player; they lose a card.
effects.coup: Choose a player; they lose a card. Nothing can stop it.

manor.intro: A rich old man has his relatives over for the night. Some are intruders in disguise who want him dead before dawn. The rest must keep him alive until 6 AM.

sections.title: Sides
items: Household: the Butler, the Guard and the Guests. Intruders: 1 with 4 players, 2 with 5–6, 3 with 7–8.
Intruders know each other. The Butler always knows where the old man was at the start of each hour. The Guard carries the flashlight.
With 4 players, the lone intruder starts holding the knife.

sections.title: Each hour
items: The night runs from 10 PM to 6 AM: 8 hours. Everyone starts in the Grand Hall; the old man starts in the Bedroom.
Move: secretly stay, or go one room up, down, left or right. Intruders can slip into any room. Nobody can stay in the Security Room two hours in a row.
Act: Secretly pick one action. It's dark — you know whether someone else is in your room and whether the old man is there, but not who, how many, or what they do.

sections.title: Actions
items: Guard: protect the old man. Attack (intruders with a weapon): hurts him if attackers outnumber guards.
Take a weapon: the knife (Kitchen), candlestick (Library) or poison (Wine Cellar). You carry one item; taking another swaps it.
Fix a camera (Library, Bedroom, Kitchen, Foyer, Garden); intruders can break one. You only see whether a camera is on from its own room or from the Security Room — nobody is told when it changes.
Watch the monitors (Security Room): see who working cameras saw this hour and whether the old man came or went — not what anyone did.
Search: pat down someone at random — you only learn whether they carry something. The Guard learns who it was and what they carry.
Flashlight (Guard): see who is in your room and what each of them does this hour. Escort: the old man follows you next hour.
Once a game, an intruder can hide their weapon for an hour: searches find nothing on them.

sections.title: Meetings
items: After midnight, after 3 AM and after every scream, the household talks it over and votes.
A majority locks a player up for the rest of the night. Their role stays secret.

sections.title: How it ends
items: Intruders win if the old man is hit twice. The first hit makes him scream — everyone learns the room, not who.
The household wins if every intruder is locked up, or the old man is alive at dawn.
At dawn the intruders get one last chance: their ringleader names the Butler. Get it right and the intruders win.

liarsdice.intro: The bar classic. Everyone shakes 5 dice and looks only at their own. Take turns bidding how many of one face are on the whole table — until someone calls a lie.

sections.title: Bidding
items: A bid is "N × face": at least N dice on the table show that face, counting everyone's dice.
The opening bid must be more than the number of players (2 players: at least 3).
Each bid must be higher: more dice, or the same number of a higher face. Faces rank 2 < 3 < 4 < 5 < 6 < 1.

sections.title: Wild 1s and zhai
items: 1s are wild: they count as any face — unless the bid is zhai (斋), when 1s count only as 1s. Calling 1s is always zhai.
Switching to zhai may keep the same number and face, since it makes the bid harder. An opening zhai bid may be as low as the number of players.
Break the fast (开斋, also called 飞): after a zhai bid, you can make 1s wild again — but you must call at least double the dice (after 3 × 4 zhai, at least 6).

sections.title: Calling a lie
items: Open (开): on your turn, instead of bidding, call the last bid a lie. Everyone's dice are revealed and counted. If there are enough, the caller drinks 1 cup; if not, the bidder does.
Split (劈): anyone — not just the player up — can split the last bid at any time. The loser drinks 2 cups.
Counter-split (反劈): the player who was split can counter. Then the loser drinks 4.

sections.title: Winning
items: After each call everyone still in shakes again, and the loser starts the next round.
Knockout: 5 cups and you're drunk — out. The last player standing wins.
Endless: nobody is ever out; cups just add up. When more than half the table votes to stop, the fewest cups win.
The host picks the mode in the lobby.
